intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that distal hereditary motor neuronopathy-14 (HMND14) is caused by mutation in the gene encoding the largest subunit of the axonal transport protein dynactin (DCTN1) on chromosome 2p13.

checks.claim: Distal hereditary motor neuronopathy-14 (HMND14) is caused by mutation in the DCTN1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Our results show that dysfunction of dynactin-mediated transport can lead to human motor neuron disease.
checks.explanation: The abstract shows that a dynactin (DCTN1) mutation causes a lower motor neuron disease. It does not use the name 'distal hereditary motor neuronopathy-14' or the word 'distal.'

checks.claim: DCTN1 encodes the largest subunit of the axonal transport protein dynactin.
checks.evidence_quote: a gene in this interval that encodes the largest subunit of the axonal transport protein dynactin
checks.explanation: Stated directly. DCTN1 is the approved symbol for this gene.

checks.claim: The DCTN1 gene is located on chromosome 2p13.
checks.evidence_quote: Here we show linkage of a lower motor neuron disease to a region of 4 Mb at chromosome 2p13. Mutation analysis of a gene in this interval that encodes the largest subunit of the axonal transport protein dynactin
checks.explanation: The gene lies in the linked 2p13 interval.

paragraphs.text: Distal hereditary motor neuronopathy-14 is a lower motor neuron disease. Puls et al. (2003) linked it to chromosome 2p13. They found a mutation in the gene encoding the largest subunit of dynactin, a protein that carries material along axons. The mutation was predicted to affect dynactin's microtubule-binding domain.

checks.evidence_quote: Here we show linkage of a lower motor neuron disease to a region of 4 Mb at chromosome 2p13.
checks.explanation: The abstract calls it a lower motor neuron disease but never gives the HMND14 or 'distal' name.

checks.explanation: The linkage to 2p13 is stated. The abstract does not name the disease as HMND14.

checks.claim: Puls et al. (2003) found a mutation in the gene encoding the largest subunit of dynactin in distal hereditary motor neuronopathy-14.
checks.evidence_quote: Mutation analysis of a gene in this interval that encodes the largest subunit of the axonal transport protein dynactin showed a single base-pair change
checks.explanation: The mutation finding is stated. The abstract does not name the disease as HMND14.

paragraphs.text: In a lower motor neuron disease linked to chromosome 2p13, Puls et al. (2003) analyzed the gene encoding the largest subunit of the axonal transport protein dynactin (DCTN1). They found a single base-pair change that caused an amino acid substitution. The substitution was predicted to distort the folding of dynactin's microtubule-binding domain. In binding assays, the mutant protein bound less to microtubules.

paragraphs.text: In binding assays by Puls et al. (2003), mutant dynactin bound less to microtubules. The authors concluded that faulty dynactin-mediated transport can lead to human motor neuron disease.
